title: Describing Automated Processes in Modern Hungarian

sections.title: No passive needed
sections.content: English technical prose is full of passives: 'the text is split into tokens', 'the answer is generated'. Modern Hungarian rarely translates them with a passive. It makes the machine the subject (*a modell tokenekre bontja a szöveget*), uses the third person plural with no subject when people do the work (*az adatokat szervereken tárolják*), uses an intransitive verb where one exists (*a mondat vektorrá alakul*, 'turns into a vector'), or uses *-va/-ve* + *van* for a resulting state (*az adatok titkosítva vannak*).

sections.title: English passive → modern Hungarian
rows: A modell tokenekre bontja a szöveget.
The text is split into tokens (by the model).
The data is stored on servers.
Each sentence is turned into a vector.
The answer is generated in seconds.

sections.content: Don't translate the English passive word for word. *A szöveg fel lett dolgozva* is colloquial, and *a szöveg a modell által kerül feldolgozásra* is officialese. Say *a modell feldolgozza a szöveget*, or, if who does it doesn't matter, *feldolgozzák a szöveget*.
